4.191 Mappable Element
Definition
A mappable element is a part of a MCAL module which can be assigned to a partition via a
reference parameter in the Base Software Module Description of the module. Mappable elements
allow the formal description on how MCAL modules are available respectively- distributed on
partitions (and thus cores).
Initiator
General
Further Explanations
The type- and scope of the functionality represented by a mappable element strongly depends on
the MCAL module. A mappable element may closely represent the hardware (e.g. a channel) but
can also represent subsets of HW units as well as groups of HW units.
Comment
Single partition MCAL driver define the complete driver as mappable element. Thus indicating
that advanced multi-partition use-cases are not supported.
Example
Adc channel, CAN controller
